title: Richard J. Reyes / WCT Current Claims and Evidence Ledger
scope: Program-level status summary. Statistical results apply only to their stated datasets, analysis choices, nulls, and background models.
interpretationRules: A symbolic or formal proof is not by itself empirical validation.
An author-run holdout or replication is not independent replication.
A p-value applies to the specified test and null/background model; it does not validate the full WCT framework.
Negative and route-closed results are retained alongside positive results.
Zenodo record-number ordering is not used as evidence of scholarly priority.

claims.claim: A training-selected log-periodic chirp-mass mode predicts the frozen GWTC-5 holdout better than the frozen smooth baseline under the declared test.
claims.supportingResult: A separately formulated KDE analysis selected k=9.7941176 and returned p=0.00089991 on the same holdout; because the holdout had already been inspected by the primary analysis, this is supporting analysis rather than an independent holdout.
claims.limitation: V1 is author-run, and V3/V4 reuse an already-inspected holdout: V4 is a structured-null robustness challenge, not independent future-catalog replication. Its phenomenological population and approximate selection models do not replace posterior-aware LVK hierarchical inference with injection-calibrated selection; WCT physical attribution is unestablished.

robustnessV4.relationshipToV1: V4 tests a V2/V3-informed fixed mode on the already-inspected 104-event GWTC-5 holdout; robustness/source-discrimination only, not a new independent holdout.
robustnessV4.nullFamily: Training-fitted continuous broken power law plus truncated Gaussian peak and monotone selection weighting (Mchirp/Mchirp_max)^gamma, without a periodic term.
robustnessV4.remainingObligation: Full posterior-aware LVK hierarchical population inference with injection-calibrated selection; genuinely unseen future-catalog evaluation against a prior frozen prediction.

claims.claim: A frozen CMS dimuon waveform remains strong under the declared prospective G2 analysis.
claims.limitation: The apparent significance is strongly background-model dependent; alternative smooth backgrounds reduce it substantially, and detector/reconstruction versus physical origin remains unresolved.

adversarialAudit.interpretation: Declared-pipeline recurrence is reproducible; significance across reasonable smooth-background models is not established.

claims.claim: The planned CMS-frequency transfer to ATLAS produced a positive independent-detector replication.
claims.limitation: The hierarchical ATLAS background route failed its frozen stability/residual-control gates before target evaluation. The untouched final CMS-frequency holdout was not run, so there is no positive or negative target-frequency replication result.

claims.claim: The Fe II log-cosine scan has a bin-stable best frequency across 120, 160, and 200 bins under the repository's declared null procedure.
claims.limitation: This is an author-run open-data result. Independent replication and the physical interpretation of the spectral structure remain separate questions.

claims.claim: Mass, force, spectra, and effective spacetime geometry emerge from confined oscillatory fields in the WCT framework.
claims.evidenceLevel: foundational proposal with mathematical, symbolic, numerical, and traceability assets
claims.result: The framework is publicly specified and has claim/equation-level audit infrastructure.
claims.limitation: The full emergence claim has not been independently established by the empirical results above. Claim-specific mathematical results and empirical tests must be evaluated separately.
